topics.title: Comedian’s Frustrations and Observations
topics.summary: A comedian discusses his job with a demanding host, Fred, including staring down, eating large amounts of food, comparing himself to Johnny Carson, and making lighthearted observations about traffic, bathroom breaks, and an older colleague's routines. The conversation includes awkward moments and self-deprecating humor.

topics.title: Lisa Gay Tremblay Reveals Underwear
topics.summary: During a radio segment, guest Lisa Gay Tremblay unexpectedly removes her underwear on air, causing immediate shock and confusion among the hosts. The conversation quickly shifts to commentary about changing entertainment standards, comparisons with past comedians like Todie Field and Phyllis Diller, and anxieties regarding program director paranoia.

topics.title: Financial Troubles and Baseball Interviews
topics.summary: During the broadcast, hosts discuss financial concerns with a guest struggling to articulate his wealth ($20 million) before transitioning into an interview with baseball player Carl Yostremski and co-author Andy Fotos about their new book ‘Yazz.’ The segment includes discussions on crowded bookstores, demanding fans, and frustrations regarding studio control.

topics.title: Boston Bonfire & Stuttering Questions
topics.summary: During a conversation at a Boston bonfire, the speaker interviews a man who makes uncomfortable and bizarre questions about baseball statistics, personal habits (including farting), Dolly's implants, and AIDS research. The discussion devolves into tangents with no clear direction before ending with a listener’s farewell message.

topics.title: Halston’s Rise and Fall – Studio 54
topics.summary: This broadcast details the life of Halston, beginning with his success designing Jackie Onassis’ iconic pillbox hat and expanding into couture. The program then covers his celebrity status at Studio 54, eventual brand sale, drug addiction struggles, and ultimately, a tragic death.

topics.title: Oscar Predictions and Radio Static
topics.summary: During a radio segment, hosts debate the best picture nominees with frustration over perceived Academy Awards irrelevance. They playfully critique celebrity interviews plagued by static and bizarre comments – including one guest admitting to smelling like a rat – while attempting to predict Oscar winners and offering humorous commentary on pop culture figures.
